name: hmdd

relevance.justification: Directly aligned with core BioThings entity types: curates experimentally-supported associations between human microRNAs (miRBase-style names, e.g. hsa-mir-21) and diseases (MeSH-style disease terms, e.g. 'Breast Neoplasms'), classified into 8 evidence categories (circulation, epigenetics, exosome, genetics, target, tissue, virus, other) with 23 evidence codes. This is exactly the kind of curated entity-relation data BioThings pending.api is built to serve.

novelty.justification: No existing BioThings API (mygene.info, mychem.info, myvariant.info, mydisease.info) curates experimentally-supported miRNA-disease associations. mydisease.info covers disease ontology/xrefs (MONDO, Disease Ontology, HPO, CTD chemical-disease/gene-disease) but nothing on miRNA-disease evidence. Checked references/existing-biothings-plugins.json and pending-api-datasources.json for any miRNA-disease or HMDD entries -- none found. HMDD v4.0 is also the only major manually-curated miRNA-disease association resource of its kind (used as ground truth by most miRNA-disease prediction papers), so novelty is unambiguous.

openness.justification: Full dataset (alldata_v4.txt, 12.8MB, 53,553 rows) is directly downloadable from the datasource's own domain with no login/registration/paywall/click-through gate (curl with a standard User-Agent returns the file directly, HTTP 200, content-type text/plain). License is non-commercial only (site: 'HMDD is free only for academic usage... For commercial usage, please Contact Dr. Qinghua Cui'; paper states 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial License'), which caps the openness score below full-open (5) but does not block academic/research ingestion.

evidence.scope: Experimentally-supported associations between human (and virus-derived) microRNAs and human diseases, spanning 8 evidence categories: circulation biomarker (diagnosis/prognosis, up/down/no-significant-change), epigenetics, exosome, genetics (overexpression/knockdown, promote/suppress, GWAS), target (gene/lncRNA/circRNA/transcription-factor), tissue expression, virus-encoded miRNA, therapeutic target, and other. Each row cites a supporting PMID and a free-text description of the finding.
evidence.overlap: No direct overlap with existing BioThings sources -- mydisease.info has disease ontology/xrefs but no miRNA-disease evidence; no BioThings API curates non-coding-RNA-disease relations of this kind.
identifiers_found: miRNA name (miRBase-style precursor/mature nomenclature, e.g. hsa-mir-21, ebv-mir-BART1)
disease name (free-text, largely MeSH-descriptor-style, e.g. 'Stomach Neoplasms')

license.name: CC BY-NC (non-commercial, academic use only)
restrictions: Non-commercial / academic use only per site notice; paper states Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial License. Commercial use requires contacting the PI (Dr. Qinghua Cui) directly. No formal CC BY-NC badge/link found on the live site itself -- flagged as a minor paper-vs-site license-presentation mismatch, though both agree on the non-commercial restriction.

api_info.record_coverage: No public REST/GraphQL API found; site only exposes an interactive search/browse UI (no documented API endpoints). No API mentioned in the NAR 2024 paper.

risks: Non-commercial license restriction (CC BY-NC / academic-only) -- flag for commercial API-consumer compatibility, consistent with several other recently ingested NAR plugins (chemprob, molbic, persade, ttd).

Disease field is free text (not a controlled-vocabulary ID like DOID/MONDO in the bulk file itself) -- cross-referencing to mydisease.info would require a separate string-matching/normalization step, not available in this bulk file.

Live site row count (53,553) is very close to but not identical to the paper's reported 53,530 -- consistent with the site's stated 'continuously updated' policy (Last-Modified: 2023-07-11, after the paper's 2023-08-19 acceptance date); treated as a minor, expected drift rather than a data-quality issue.

No miRBase accession/MIMAT IDs in the bulk file -- miRNA names are HMDD's own curated nomenclature strings, some of which (e.g. cluster names like '14q32 cluster', 'C19MC cluster') do not map cleanly to a single miRBase entry.
next_actions: Proceed to plugin generation using alldata_v4.txt as the sole bulk-download source
